c: Polycarbonate moulds clean, dry, 22–24 °C; polish cavities with cotton wool (gloss).
Working temperatures: dark 31–32 °C, milk 29–30 °C, white 28–29 °C; check with a test strip (sets glossy in 5 min at 18 °C).
Shell 1–1.2 mm: fill, tap out air, invert, scrape clean; set at 16 °C.
Pipe ganache at 27–28 °C max (hotter melts the shell); leave 2 mm for the cap.
Crystallise 12–24 h at 16–18 °C, RH < 60%; cap with tempered chocolate, transfer sheet on top, scrape.
Release after 30 min at 10 °C; clean release = good temper. Dull spots = poor temper or cold mould.
Weigh 10 pieces per batch (target ± 0.5 g); cut 1 to check shell thickness and filling ratio (70:30 filling:shell).
Fat bloom = warm storage; sugar bloom = condensation; cracked shells = filling too cold/expanding; leaking = thin cap.
Record batch, Aw target, best-before and allergens on each tray.

c: Piped bonbon ganache: dark 1 : 1.4 · milk 1 : 1.8 · white 1 : 2.2 (softer, set in shell).
Fruit ganache: replace cream with purée + 10–15% butter; keep total water ≤ 20%.
Target Aw 0.75–0.80 for 4–6 weeks at 16–18 °C; > 0.85 = 2 weeks max.
Invert sugar 5–8% of ganache weight lowers Aw and keeps it soft; glucose 5–10% for texture and gloss; sorbitol optional.
Alcohol 2–4% (40% vol spirit) adds 1–2 weeks shelf life; add below 35 °C.
Bring cream + sugars to 85 °C; pour over chocolate in 3 additions; stick-blend without air to a glossy emulsion at 35–40 °C.
Add soft butter at 33–35 °C; pipe at 27–28 °C or frame at 30 °C.
Split (oily) ganache: blend in 5% warm milk or cream; grainy = too cold, warm to 34 °C and re-blend.
Melt colour at 40–45 °C; shake well; temper by cooling to 29–30 °C (or seed 1% cocoa butter silk).
Airbrush/spray gun at 29–30 °C; moulds at 20–22 °C (too cold = streaks, too warm = no release).
Splatter: flick a stiff brush 20 cm from the mould; brush: gloved finger swirl; layer dark colours last (they show first).
Always back-spray white over bright colours on dark chocolate; scrape cavity rims clean.
Let colour crystallise 10 min before shelling; transfer sheets go on the cap, shiny side up.
